name: Lamb Weston Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Lamb Weston is one of the world's largest producers of frozen potato products — fries, specialty cuts and appetizers — for quick-service restaurant chains, foodservice distributors and retailers. It sells under its own Lamb Weston, Grown in Idaho and Alexia brands, private labels and licensed brands. Founded in 1950, spun off from Conagra in November 2016 and headquartered in Eagle, Idaho, it generated FY2026 (May year-end) net sales of $6.61B. It is executing a 'Focus to Win' restructuring under CEO Mike Smith following pressure from activist investor Jana Partners.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The past five years were defined by capacity expansion and buying out European and Argentine joint venture partners — net sales rose from $3.67B (FY2021) to $6.61B (FY2026) — rather than new product categories; the company then had to close its Connell, WA plant in October 2024 amid overcapacity [2][4]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI-driven savings were found [4]. Market Share (1/2): Lamb Weston is one of the world's biggest frozen fry makers, and North America volume grew 7% in Q1 FY2027 for a seventh straight quarter of volume growth, but international sales fell 8% and no share data was disclosed [1][4]. Pipeline (0/2): FY2027 guidance was raised to low-single-digit sales growth, but no next-generation product pipeline with timelines was found [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports R&D-to-revenue of 0%, with no separately disclosed R&D spend [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Lamb Weston's purpose, 'Seeing possibilities in potatoes,' is specific to its category and has some character, but it describes a product focus rather than a deeper purpose and has not been validated by distinctive strategic choices [6]. Community Impact (1/2): The company publishes annual ESG reports, reports reusing 496M gallons of water (FY2022), and a sustainability summary cites about $830,000 donated to food banks and community programs — general corporate philanthropy [6][7]. Employee Retention (0/2): The company cut about 4% of its global workforce and closed the Connell plant, affecting about 375 workers, in its 2024 restructuring [4]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful insider buying was found; ownership change was instead driven by activist Jana Partners (5%+) [4].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on all 10 dividend metrics. At target: 5-year revenue CAGR of 12.5% ($3.67B in FY2021 to $6.61B in FY2026), forward P/E of about 16.7x (derived from the $53.29 price and the $3.20 midpoint of company adjusted EPS guidance of $3.05-3.35), 10 consecutive years of dividends since the 2016 spin-off (2x weight), and a 5-year dividend CAGR of about 10.0% (2x weight) [1][2][3]. Partial credit: TTM ROE of 14.1% (0.94), 8 consecutive years of dividend increases (0.80; third-party counts range from 6 to 9) and TTM revenue growth of 2.6% (0.75) [2][3]. Drags: D/E of 217% (0.36), TTM net margin of only 3.8% (0.19) and a GAAP payout ratio of 81.6% (0.31) [2]. Weighted score 9.35/12 → 8. Liquidity floor cleared: 1.91M avg volume × $53.29 ≈ $102M/day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Lamb Weston grows, processes, freezes and ships potatoes through a physical network of plants, cold storage and long-term grower contracts — AI cannot substitute for french fries or the manufacturing that produces them [1][5]. No analyst commentary was found flagging AI disruption risk; the company's real risks are restaurant traffic, overcapacity and input-cost inflation, not AI [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue or quantified AI deployment was found [4].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, Lamb Weston is currently playing a defensive, finite game: after overbuilding capacity and stumbling on execution, it is cutting costs, closing plants and reshaping its board under activist pressure. A 75-year heritage and an internal CEO provide continuity, but recent decisions are driven by quarterly pressure rather than a lived Just Cause.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Seeing possibilities in potatoes' is a pleasant brand line, not a vision of a better future people would sacrifice for [6]. Recent strategy ('Focus to Win' prioritization of markets and channels) is framed around efficiency and returns rather than a cause [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The 2024 restructuring cut about 4% of the global workforce and closed the Connell plant, affecting about 375 workers [4]. That came alongside a CEO transition and activist demands to overhaul the board or sell the company over 'chronic mis-execution' — conditions that push employees into self-protection [4]. Mike Smith's internal promotion (with the company since 2007) is a partial stabilizer.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that frames McCain, Simplot or Agristo as rivals to learn from. In the Oregon nitrate groundwater lawsuit, Lamb Weston's response has been to shift blame to neighboring processor J.R. Simplot [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The company has evolved — spinning off from Conagra in 2016, consolidating joint ventures in Europe and Argentina to become a global player, and now refocusing under 'Focus to Win' [1][2]. These are incremental moves within frozen potatoes, not a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Recent decisions — plant closures, a $55M cost-savings program, and board changes after Jana Partners' campaign — respond to shareholder pressure and short-term earnings misses rather than sacrificing near-term results for long-term capability [4]. Adjusted EBITDA still fell to $286M from $302M in Q1 FY2027 [1].

investment_thesis: Lamb Weston is a scaled global leader in an essential, AI-proof category, and its turnaround is gaining traction. Q1 FY2027 adjusted EPS of $0.75 beat guidance on North America net sales up 5% (volume up 7%, a seventh straight quarter of volume growth), and management raised FY2027 guidance to low-single-digit sales growth, $1.125-1.215B adjusted EBITDA and $3.05-3.35 adjusted EPS [1]. At $53.29 the stock trades at about 16.7x the guidance midpoint, yields 2.83%, and has a 10-year dividend record with a roughly 10% 5-year dividend CAGR, while generating about $700M of TTM free cash flow to equity [2][3]. Activist Jana Partners' involvement adds a catalyst — board change or even a sale of the company [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that GAAP fundamentals are deteriorating under a leveraged balance sheet. Q1 FY2027 GAAP EPS fell to $0.21 from $0.46, FY2026 GAAP EPS of $2.09 was down 17% and 58% below FY2024's $5.01, and TTM net margin is just 3.8% [1][2]. D/E of 217% and net debt of about 4.1x EBITDA leave little room for error, and the 81.6% GAAP payout ratio limits dividend growth [2]. International sales fell 8% with sharply lower European EBITDA on industry overcapacity, and management flags unexpected inflation in input and freight costs [1]. An August 2026 federal lawsuit alleging nitrate contamination of Eastern Oregon drinking water adds legal and reputational risk [5].
key_catalysts: Delivery on raised FY2027 guidance ($1.125-1.215B adjusted EBITDA, $3.05-3.35 adjusted EPS), building on seven straight quarters of North American volume growth [1]
Jana Partners-driven board changes or a strategic review, including the potential sale of the company that the activist has called for [4]
'Focus to Win' cost actions and capacity rationalization restoring margins from the 19.4% TTM gross margin as industry overcapacity clears [1][2]
key_risks: Leverage: D/E of 217% and net debt of about 4.1x EBITDA, with interest coverage of only 2.9x, limit flexibility if restaurant traffic weakens [2]
International weakness: Q1 FY2027 international sales fell 8% with lower European volumes, higher manufacturing costs and inflation squeezing EBITDA [1]
Environmental litigation: the August 2026 federal lawsuit by Eastern Oregon residents alleging nitrate contamination of drinking-water groundwater [5]
